title: Quantum Formulation of the Spinterface Model
abstract: We present a fully quantum formulation of the spinterface model for the chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS) effect, implemented within the non-equilibrium Green's function (NEGF) formalism. The model consists of a gold atom hosting a localised magnetic moment, coupled to a chiral molecular chain with Rashba spin-orbit coupling, and contacted by two non-magnetic leads. The magnetic moment is determined self-consistently from the non-equilibrium electronic distribution, and the spin-resolved transmission is computed from the mean-field Hamiltonian. We show that the interfacial magnetic moment and the chiral Rashba term cooperate to produce large current polarisations that reproduce the key experimental signatures of CISS: high polarisation, a threshold emergence at four total sites followed by interference-modulated growth with chain length, thermal suppression, and sign reversal upon chirality inversion. The central new result of this work is a clean separation of the CISS effect into an even (achiral) and an odd (chiral) contribution to the spin current, $I_{S_z}(φ) = I_{S_z}^{\rm even}(φ) + I_{S_z}^{\rm odd}(φ)$. We demonstrate that $I_{S_z}^{\rm odd}$ vanishes exactly at fixed $m_z$ for chains of fewer than four sites and becomes non-zero for chains of four or more sites, with the smallest junction exhibiting a non-zero odd part being the four-site geometry (one gold atom plus three molecular sites). The odd part arises from reciprocity breaking in a device that is simultaneously chiral, magnetically asymmetric (moment on the gold end only), and long enough to support two or more Rashba-active bonds. This provides a direct, parameter-free test of whether an observed spin signal is genuinely chiral or arises from an achiral spin-valve mechanism.
summary: This work develops a quantum mechanical model for the CISS effect using the NEGF formalism. It introduces a crucial even-odd decomposition of the spin current, allowing researchers to isolate the purely chiral contribution. This provides a rigorous, symmetry-based test to confirm if an observed spin signal truly originates from molecular chirality rather than simple magnetic asymmetry.
main_problem: To provide a fully quantum formulation of the chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS) effect in molecular junctions.
main_result: The spin current can be cleanly decomposed into even (achiral) and odd (chiral) contributions, providing a parameter-free diagnostic to distinguish genuine chiral signals from achiral spin-valve effects.
method: The study employs the non-equilibrium Green's function (NEGF) formalism to calculate spin-resolved transmission through the spinterface model.
model_or_system: The model consists of a gold atom with a localized magnetic moment coupled to a chiral molecular chain featuring Rashba spin-orbit coupling, contacted by non-magnetic leads.
key_observables: Spin current polarization, specifically the odd part of the spin current, $I_{S_z}^{m odd}(\varphi)$.
important_parameters: Chain length ($L$), magnetic moment ($m_z$), and the chiral coupling strength ($\lambda_R$).
main_assumptions: The magnetic moment is treated self-consistently using a mean-field approximation, and the analysis often relies on the single-particle picture.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate spin density profiles along the chain, comparing fixed-field and rotating-field models, and showing the emergence of the odd spin current component at sufficient chain length.
paper_structure: The paper develops the NEGF framework for the spinterface model, derives the even-odd decomposition of the spin current, and uses this decomposition to analyze the physical requirements (chirality, asymmetry, length) necessary for the odd, chiral contribution to manifest.
why_interesting: The explicit separation of spin current into even and odd parts provides a powerful, symmetry-based diagnostic tool applicable to open quantum systems and mesoscopic transport phenomena.

figures.caption: Figure 1. Schematic of the spinterface junction. A gold atom (Au) carrying a mean-ﬁeld moment mA sits between a non- magnetic left lead and a chiral molecular chain of L sites, coupled to the leads through ΓL and ΓR under an applied bias V . The chain carries a nearest-neighbour hopping tmol and a Rashba spin-ﬂip iλR sin(φ/2) per bond, with φ the twist angle per bond; the Au–molecule bond is spin-diagonal. The eﬀective ﬁeld Beﬀacting on the gold moment is determined self-consistently from the interfacial spin accumulation. Figure 3. Bias dependence of the spin-split gold on-site en- ergies εA↑(solid blue) and εA↓(dashed red), together with the bias window [µR, µL] (shaded green). The two levels are separated by ∆εA = (Jel + 2J′ p)mz, which is of order 0.5 eV in our parameters. The progressive capture of the spin-split levels by the bias window explains the bias dependence of the current polarisation in Fig. 2(b).

Figure 2. Transport characteristics of the spinterface junction at T = 300 K. (a) Spin-resolved current I↑(solid blue) and I↓(dashed red) as a function of bias voltage. The current is antisymmetric under bias reversal and the two spin chan- nels diﬀer in magnitude over the entire range. (b) Current polarisation PJ = (I↑−I↓)/(I↑+ I↓) as a function of bias. The polarisation peaks at intermediate bias where one spin channel lies fully inside the bias window, and decreases at large bias when both channels contribute. The shaded band indicates the historical experimental range of 60-70%; recent experiments reach up to 85-90% in supramolecular nanoﬁbers and topological knots.

Figure 4. Spin current ISz = I↑−I↓as a function of the chirality angle φ over the full range [−π, π], for chain lengths L = 1 (dark blue) to L = 6 (yellow), at V = 1.0 V. For L = 1 the spin current is constant (no Rashba term). For L = 2 it is nearly symmetric in φ (collinear geometry, no handedness). For L ≥3 the curve becomes strongly antisymmetric: revers- ing the sign of φ reverses the sign of the spin current, which is the direct signature of chirality-induced spin selectivity.

Figure 5. Decomposition of the spin current into even and odd parts with respect to the chirality angle φ. (a) Even part, Ieven Sz (φ), which is present for all chain lengths and insensitive to the sign of φ: this is the achiral spin-valve signal. (b) Odd part, Iodd Sz (φ), which vanishes exactly at ﬁxed mz for L = 1, is essentially zero for L = 2, and grows rapidly for L ≥3. (c) Maximum magnitude of the odd part, maxφ |Iodd Sz |, as a function of chain length L, showing the emergence of handedness at L = 3 (four total sites).
